claims: The CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) is a real-time market index.
The CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) represents the market's expectation of 30-day forward-looking volatility of the S&P 500® Index (SPX).
The VIX is calculated using SPX option prices.
The VIX generally has an inverse relationship with the S&P 500.
The VIX uses a 30-day, constant, weighted measure of SPX options with Friday expirations.
You cannot buy the VIX directly.
Investors trade the VIX through futures, options, and exchange-traded products (ETPs).
As of mid-April 2026, the VIX dropped to around 16–18 levels from higher levels.
The VIX experienced a 44% crash in the three weeks ending April 17, 2026.
The VIX hit a nine-week low of 16.87.
